analysis.title: US EQUITIES COLOR: EVERYTHING RALLY
key_insights: Broad 'everything rally' on 9 Nov 2026: S&P +2.35% to 7,549, NDX +3.4% to 27,907, R2K +3.18% to 2,841, Dow +2.15% to 52,389. SOX +6.8% despite NVDA -4.3%. 420+ S&P names closed up (423 of 500 per the derivs section).
The rally followed a volatile week of election-driven rotations, pressure on investor performance, and large cuts in gross and net exposure, with a big cut in tech length specifically.
Crude fell about 5% to roughly $85-87 on further Iran de-escalation. Trump said extensive strikes on Iran are 'highly unlikely', conditional on Iran signing 'a very strong agreement'.

The desk saw a mix of covering and long buying across tech, excluding NVDA after weekend headlines. The market is hesitant to give the all clear ahead of CPI tomorrow (GIR at +16bps for core MoM) and CRWV/NBIS earnings later this week.

Desk activity was 5 on a 1-10 scale. Asset manager flows were roughly flat, with demand in tech and financials against supply in communication services. Hedge funds were net buyers, largely through macro products.

GS PB data: US Info Tech net allocation is 14.4% of total US net market value, in the 1st/1st/3rd percentiles on 1-year/3-year/5-year lookbacks. Semis positioning has almost fully round-tripped in 2026.
A GIR note calls semis 'clearly oversold' and favors AVGO and NVDA (valuations imply no growth past 2027), AMAT and LRCX (semicap), and SK Hynix and Samsung (trading below total tangible book).

SPX closing imbalance was $4B to sell. CTAs are estimated to be larger sellers of US equities in every scenario this week. The desk is watching the medium-term threshold at 7548, which the index closed just above.
About 90% of S&P 500 companies are in their buyback open window, with about 93% expected by the end of the week. Early November strength fits historical seasonality.
Derivatives: VVIX had its 3rd sharpest daily decline in 20 years, and vols and skew were crushed across the board. VIX fell to 19.92.
Flow: SPY downside was unwound alongside upside buying. GS customers sold 56k 13Nov 730/715 put spreads and 22k 27Nov 720/700 put spreads to buy 28k SPY 18Dec 775/800 call spreads.
Single-name flow: customers rolled 52.5k of an NVDA-style 19Feb 210/255 call spread (name not stated in the text) down to 195/245. Options in the name saw two-way flow after the NVDA news.

The desk likes IWM upside into month-end: November seasonality is strong, CTAs are buyers, positioning is low, the short base is high, and IWM looks like the cheapest vol on the board. The 27Nov 290 calls outright screen attractive, and the straddle to the end of the week is 1.50%.
